_note: Will and estate papers of Henrietta S. Duterte, 1903-04. Added 2026-11-14 from Michiko's screenshots of the Ancestry images (images 80, 87, 91, 93 of 318 and one will page; the scans themselves are Ancestry's and are not on the site). Read by Claude from the screenshots; only some pages were supplied, so the executors' names, the residuary clause and the rest of the will are not entered. Attendee 359991 is the merged 'Henrietta Duterte' record. Sarah Ball is the newspaper record 'Sarah Bowers-Ball' (the will's surname reads Ball or Bell; the 1873 will of John C. Bowers names their sister Sarah Bowers). Joseph T. Seth and Lucretia Miller already have records as Institute for Colored Youth students of 1864. T. J. Minton, attorney for the executors, is taken to be Theophilus J. Minton the lawyer. Jerome Jackson and George Custus get fresh records (new:duterte1903).

events.name: Will and estate of Henrietta S. Duterte, undertaker, 517 and 519 South Ninth Street (1903-04)
events.description: Henrietta S. Duterte made her will on December 3, 1903, and it was proved on December 31, 1903. By then her undertaking business was at No. 519 South Ninth Street, a one-story office, beside her three-story brick dwelling at No. 517, with a coach house and stable at the rear on South Darien Street. She had been forced to sell 634 Lombard Street when that block was condemned in 1893 to build Starr Garden (Michiko Quinones, 1838 Black Metropolis). She left the business to her nephew Joseph T. Seth. || From the will: to her sister Sarah Ball (the surname is written Ball or Bell), five hundred dollars and the furniture in the back sitting room and two second-story rooms of No. 838 Lombard Street; to Jerome Jackson and George Custus, one hundred and fifty dollars each 'as a mark of my appreciation of their length of service in my employ', provided they were still in her service; to her nephew Joseph T. Seth, 'the good will and stock of my undertaking business now located at No. 519 South Ninth Street in the City of Philadelphia, including my horses, carriages, wagons, hearses, harness, coffins, caskets, ice boxes and other contents of my office, shop and stables'. Only part of the will has been read. || The property, from the tax appraisement and its plan: 'Premises situate Nos 517 and 519 South 9th Street ... 3 story brick house 2 story brick stable and coach house in rear lot 41 feet 7 inches by 188 feet', valued at $10,000 less a $3,000 mortgage. No. 519 and the lot and stable behind No. 517 were devised to Joseph T. Seth. Her niece Lucretia C. Miller, aged 54, had a life estate in No. 517. || The inventory, sworn March 31, 1904, by appraisers Robert A. Hopkins and Harry M. Kelley: contents of the undertaker's office and store-room (desk, chairs, stools, ice boxes), $50; one large and one small black hearse, $300; two carriages, $200; six horses, harness, feed chest and stable implements, $200; two wagons, $75; burial lots in Eden, Olive and Merion Cemeteries, $300; household furniture and wearing apparel, $50; total $1,175. || The executors' account lists the business's bills for the last weeks of 1903 (A. and J. Janton, the National Casket Co., Boyertown, carriage hire), a payment to the Union Benevolent Society of the Crucifixion, and a counsel fee of $150 to T. J. Minton, who signs as attorney for the executors. || Source: will of Henrietta S. Duterte, dated December 3, 1903 and proved December 31, 1903, case no. 2239 (Wills, No. 2234-2258, 1903), with the inventory sworn March 31, 1904, the tax appraisement and the executors' account. Ancestry.com, Pennsylvania, U.S., Wills and Probate Records, 1683-1993 (Lehi, UT: Ancestry.com Operations, Inc., 2015).
